newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker urges FASB to finish derivatives rules.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker urges FASB to finish derivatives rules.

text.p: Congressman John Dingell, the senior Democrat on the House Commerce Committee, urged the Financial Accounting Standards Board to hurry up and finish new, controversial derivatives accounting rules it has been drafting for several years.

The Michigan lawmaker's request, in a June 17 letter to the independent standards-setting board, comes a year after the group began debating its latest draft of rules for companies to use to account for derivatives and other privately negotiated transactions to offset risks.
Many derivatives industry participants, as well as some leading Republican lawmakers, have opposed the latest draft and earlier versions.

"If the board re-exposes the draft, it is entirely possible that respondents will call for more major revisions and this process could continue indefinitely," Dingell wrote to the board's outgoing chairman, Dennis Beresford.
Dingell warned that the "continued atmosphere of uncertainty" might discourage firms from using derivatives.
"That would not be consistent with the public interest or the protection of investors," Dingell wrote.
The accounting board is considered unlikely to finalize the rules by June 30, a deadline the panel in December promised the Securities and Exchange Commission it would keep.
An FASB official said in April that the panel might have to "re-expose" the draft, or release a new proposal, rather than issue final rules.
Beresford reportedly acknowledged last month that the board would not meet the June 30 deadline.
